title: Perioperative Vitamin C to Reduce Persistent Pain After Total Knee Arthroplasty
official: PeRiOperative VItamin C to Reduce perSistent paIn After tOtal kNee Arthroplasty (PROVISION): a Multicentre Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Phase III Multicentre, parallel-group, blinded, 1:1 randomized controlled trial to determine the effect of perioperative vitamin C supplementation on reducing the prevalence of persistent pain 3 months after total knee arthroplasty.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients \>18 years old
* Undergoing a unilateral or simultaneous bilateral primary total knee arthroplasty for advanced osteoarthritis of the knee.

Exclusion Criteria:

* TKA for infection (septic joint), fracture, ankylosing spondylitis, lupus, or psoriatic arthritis
* History of kidney stones, acute or chronic renal failure, hemochromatosis, or glucose-6-phosphate deficiency
* Unlikely to comply with follow-up (e.g., no fixed address, plans to move out of town)
* Language difficulties that would impede valid completion of questionnaires
* Planned staged bilateral TKA
* Treating surgeon deems patient inappropriate for inclusion in trial
* Unwilling to abstain from non-study vitamin C during trial except for up to 100 mg/day contained in a routinely used multivitamin
* Pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study
